long_biography.plain_text:
At 29, Emilio Fernando Azcárraga Jean took charge of Televisa with a heavy debt load and an oversized payroll. He had entered the group through operations at a Tijuana television station, later overseeing programming and company-wide operations. Once in charge, he sold non-core assets, reduced costs and brought in investors, stabilising the family business.

Beyond free-to-air television, Azcárraga directed investment in cable, satellite and telecommunications while seeking a wider Spanish-speaking audience in the United States. After two decades as chief executive, he moved away from daily management. Televisa later combined its content business with Univision in 2022, leaving Grupo Televisa focused on connectivity while retaining a substantial shareholding in the new Spanish-language media company.
